limitations_and_boundaries: The study focuses on the zebrafish blastoderm, a non-confluent tissue; applicability to confluent tissues may differ.
Rigidity percolation theory predicts critical point and linear response, but quantitative viscosity values require more detailed modeling of nonlinear and time-dependent properties.
2D analysis was used, but 3D connectivity patterns were similar; however, 3D rigidity percolation critical point may differ.
Perturbation experiments were limited to E-cadherin knockdown and cell fate changes; other adhesion molecules or mechanical factors were not systematically tested.
Hallmarks of criticality were demonstrated, but finite size effects and measurement precision may limit detection in other systems.
